local_trade_licensing_preserved|None.reason: Preserving existing local trade licensing standards (electricians, plumbers, etc.) maintains additional layers of licensing requirements that most states don't explicitly codify, adding burden.

locum_tenens_permit_available|None.reason: Providing a locum tenens temporary permit creates an additional pathway for out-of-state physicians to practice, lowering barriers to entry for substituting practitioners.

long_term_compliance_qualifier_waiver_ye.reason: Allowing long-term compliant businesses to maintain licensure without a qualifier after five years reduces ongoing burdens, making it more permissive than states that don't address this.

lpn_supervision_requirements|None.reason: Mandating that LPNs work under supervision of an RN, APRN, physician, PA, or dentist imposes a supervision requirement; most states don't codify this, making it more restrictive.

master_electrician_engineering_degree_pa.reason: Providing an engineering degree pathway with only one year of practical experience as an alternative to the standard apprenticeship lowers barriers for qualified engineers, making it more permissive.

master_electrician_journeyman_experience.reason: Requiring four years of journeyman experience to become a master electrician is a substantial requirement that most states don't address, imposing a higher barrier.

master_electrician_trade_school_degree_p.reason: Providing a trade school degree pathway with two years of journeyman experience as an alternative to the standard route lowers barriers for trade school graduates.

master_plumber_supervisory_experience_re.reason: Requiring two years of supervisory experience as a journeyman before obtaining a master plumber license is an additional barrier most states don't impose.

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.reason: Capping the combined number of APRNs and PAs a delegating physician may supervise at eight imposes a restriction on practice scope and limits how many practitioners can work under a single physician.

mobile_dental_facility_registration_requ.reason: Requires operators of mobile dental facilities to obtain a certificate of registration from the board before operating, a requirement most states do not impose.

multistate_license_option_available|None.reason: Offers applicants the option of a multistate license, giving nurses more flexibility to practice across states — most states don't address this.

national_electrical_code_reference|None.reason: Referencing the National Electrical Code for definitional purposes is an organizational/definitional choice with no clear directional burden.

natural_gas_appliance_certification_requ.reason: Requiring training and certification before performing natural gas appliance work adds a barrier most states don't impose.

nonresident_temporary_practice_allowed|N.reason: Explicitly allowing nonresident temporary practice creates a permissive pathway for out-of-state practitioners that most states don't provide, lowering barriers to entry for nonresidents.

nurse_aide_registry_maintained|None.reason: Requires the board to maintain a nurse aide registry including federal abuse/neglect findings — an accountability mechanism most states don't codify, adding oversight burden.

profession_specific.pain_management_educ.reason: Not requiring pain management education as a condition of licensure or practice removes a continuing education or training burden that the majority of states (20) impose, making practice easier.

profession_specific.pediatric_sedation_e.reason: Not requiring a pediatric sedation endorsement removes a credential burden that the minority of states imposing it place on practitioners, making practice easier relative to those states.

profession_specific.peer_review_records_.reason: Not providing privilege for peer review records means those records are discoverable and admissible in civil or criminal actions, exposing practitioners to greater legal risk than in states where such records are privileged.

profession_specific.peer_review_required.reason: Making peer review discretionary ('may require') rather than mandatory for firm renewal is more permissive than the majority of states that require peer review as a condition of renewal.

profession_specific.pharmaceutical_certi.reason: Not requiring pharmaceutical certification means optometrists face fewer barriers to prescribing drugs compared to the majority of states (44/50) that require such certification.

profession_specific.physician_assistant_.reason: Requiring direct supervision of physician assistants is more burdensome than the collaborative practice agreement model used by most states, limiting PA autonomy and imposing stricter oversight requirements.

Requiring a board-approved job description for physician assistant supervision adds an administrative approval step beyond the collaborative practice agreement model used by most states, imposing a greater regulatory burden.

profession_specific.plumbing_trade_geogr.reason: Sets the geographic limit at only 2 feet outside the building, narrower than the majority value of 5 feet, meaning plumbing jurisdiction extends less far and more work may fall outside licensed plumber scope — but from the practitioner's perspective, a smaller scope means less work covered, which is more restrictive on the trade's domain.

Sets the geographic limit at 20 feet beyond the building foundation, much larger than the majority value of 5 feet, expanding the scope of work covered under the plumbing license and giving practitioners a broader domain.
Sets the geographic limit at 3 feet outside the building walls, narrower than the majority value of 5 feet, restricting the scope of work covered under the plumbing license.

profession_specific.podiatric_assistant_.reason: Not authorizing podiatric assistants (and requiring that any employee administering physical modalities be a licensed health care provider) is more restrictive than the majority of states (20) that do authorize podiatric assistants, limiting practice flexibility.
The majority requires direct supervision on premises. General supervision is a lower level of oversight, reducing the burden on practitioners and allowing more independent practice.

profession_specific.practice_privilege_n.reason: Requiring out-of-state CPAs to conform to board-promulgated rules before practicing in the state (rather than allowing practice privilege with no notice) is more restrictive than the majority of states that permit practice privilege without prior notice or approval.

profession_specific.qualifier_cessation_.reason: A 10-day notification window is far shorter than the 90-day majority standard, imposing a significantly tighter compliance burden on practitioners.
A 15-day notification window is much shorter than the majority value of 90 days, imposing a stricter and more burdensome timeline on licensees.
A 30-day notification window is shorter than the 90-day majority standard, giving practitioners less time to comply and thus imposing a tighter burden.
A 60-day notification/replacement window is shorter than the majority value of 90 days, giving businesses less time and imposing a stricter burden.
A 7-day notification window is much shorter than the majority value of 90 days, giving businesses far less time to comply and thus imposing a stricter burden.

profession_specific.qualifier_replacemen.reason: 100 days exceeds the majority grace period of 90 days, giving businesses more time to find a replacement qualifier before facing penalties.
120 days exceeds the majority grace period of 90 days, allowing businesses more time to find a replacement qualifier before license cancellation.
180 days (6 months) is double the majority grace period of 90 days, providing businesses significantly more time to replace a qualifying party.
A 30-day grace period to replace a qualifier is shorter than the majority value of 90 days, giving businesses less time and thus imposing a stricter requirement.
Provides only a 45-day grace period to replace a qualifier, shorter than the majority value of 60 days, imposing a tighter deadline and greater burden on licensees.
A 60-day grace period to replace a qualifying agent is shorter than the 90-day majority standard, giving businesses less time and thus imposing a greater burden.
Provides a 90-day grace period to replace a qualifier, longer than the majority value of 60 days, giving licensees more time and thus a lower burden when a qualifier departs.

Requiring notification within 10 days is a shorter window than the majority value of 15 days, giving licensees less time to comply — but from the practitioner's burden perspective, a shorter notice period is slightly more restrictive. However, 10 days vs. 15 days means the licensee must act faster, which is more burdensome. This is more_restrictive.
Requires notice of qualifier cessation within 14 days, slightly shorter than the majority value of 15 days, imposing a marginally tighter deadline on licensees.

Requiring notification within 30 days is longer than the majority value of 15 days for notice, but the notice period itself is still a burden. However, 30 days > 15 days means more time to notify, which is more permissive for the notice requirement. Wait — a longer notice deadline means the practitioner has more time before they must act, which is more permissive.
5 days is less than the majority notice requirement of 15 days, giving businesses less time to report the loss of a qualified individual, which is more burdensome.
Allows 60 days to provide notice of qualifier replacement, much longer than the majority value of 15 days, giving licensees more time and imposing a lower burden.

7 days is less than the majority notice requirement of 15 days, but a shorter notice window is more burdensome on businesses. However, a shorter deadline to notify is more restrictive as it gives less time to report. This is more restrictive than the 15-day majority.
Allowing 90 days to notify and replace a qualifier is much longer than the majority value of 15 days, giving licensees more time and reducing the burden.

profession_specific.rd_credential_accept.reason: Not accepting the RD credential in lieu of state requirements means practitioners must separately satisfy state qualifications even if they hold the national RD credential, adding burden compared to the majority of states that accept it.

profession_specific.residential_building.reason: Defines a residential jobsite as up to 8 attached dwellings, much higher than the majority cap of 2 units, meaning more projects qualify under the residential category and fewer require additional licensing burdens.

profession_specific.retired_license_stat.reason: Most states that address this offer a retired license status (allowing fee waivers or reduced requirements for retired practitioners). This state does not offer that option, meaning retired licensees face the same full requirements as active ones — a higher burden.

profession_specific.right_of_rescission_.reason: Only 1 business day to rescind is shorter than the majority 3-day window, giving property owners less time to cancel and placing less burden on contractors.

A 10-day rescission window is longer than the majority 3-day window, giving property owners more time to cancel — this is more permissive for owners but more burdensome for contractors, making it more restrictive on practitioners.

profession_specific.safe_harbor_disclaim.reason: Lacking safe harbor disclaimer language for nonlicensees means unlicensed persons have no statutory protection for offering bookkeeping or related services, which is more restrictive than the 29 states that provide such a safe harbor.

profession_specific.small_project_dollar.reason: A $100 threshold is far below the majority value of $1,000, meaning almost no work qualifies as minor and nearly all electrical work requires a license.
A $10,000 threshold before contractor licensing is required is much higher than the majority value of $1,000, exempting far more projects and reducing the number of people who must be licensed.
A $2,500 threshold is higher than the majority value of $1,000, exempting more projects from licensing requirements.
A $5,000 threshold is five times the majority value of $1,000, meaning more small projects are exempt from licensing requirements, reducing the regulatory burden.
A $7,000 threshold is seven times the majority value of $1,000, exempting a much broader range of projects from licensing requirements.
A $7,200 annual aggregate threshold is much higher than the majority value of $1,000, exempting more casual/handyman work from licensing requirements.
Sets the small project exemption threshold at $2,500, higher than the majority value of $1,000, meaning more projects are exempt from licensing requirements and fewer practitioners are regulated.

Sets the small project exemption threshold at $25,000, far above the majority value of $1,000, exempting a very large range of projects from licensing requirements and reducing the regulatory burden on many practitioners.
Sets the small project exemption threshold at $7,000, well above the majority value of $1,000, exempting significantly more projects and practitioners from licensing requirements.
Sets the small project exemption threshold at $7,200 annually, far above the majority value of $1,000, exempting many more practitioners from licensing requirements.

profession_specific.small_project_exempt.reason: A $10,000 exemption threshold is much higher than the $1,000 majority threshold, meaning more small projects fall outside the licensing requirement and fewer practitioners are regulated.
A $1,500 threshold is higher than the majority value of $1,000, exempting slightly more projects from licensing requirements.
A $2,500 threshold is higher than the majority value of $1,000, exempting more projects from licensing requirements and thus being more permissive.
A $50,000 threshold before a license is required is far higher than the majority value of $1,000, meaning far fewer projects require a license and the exemption covers much more work.
A $7,000 threshold is much higher than the majority value of $1,000, exempting a much broader range of projects from licensing requirements.
A $7,200 annual compensation threshold is much higher than the majority value of $1,000, exempting significantly more work from licensing requirements.

profession_specific.specialist_license_a.reason: Most states (27) offer a specialist license pathway. This state does not offer one, yet still restricts specialty advertising/holding out, leaving dentists with fewer formal options to distinguish their specialty practice.

profession_specific.specialty_advertisin.reason: Not requiring a specialty advertising disclaimer is a lower burden than the majority of states that do require one, though the underlying restriction on claiming specialty status still exists.

profession_specific.specialty_practice_s.reason: Most states (13) restrict a specialist's scope of practice to their specialty. This state explicitly does not restrict a specialist's ability to practice in other areas, giving licensed dentists broader practice freedom.

profession_specific.state_preempts_local.reason: The state does not preempt local registration fees, meaning contractors may face additional local fee requirements on top of state requirements, increasing the overall burden compared to states that do preempt local fees.

profession_specific.supervised_clinical_.reason: Most states that address this require a supervised clinical internship. This state does not, lowering the barrier to entry for optometrists seeking to administer oral pharmaceutical agents.

profession_specific.surgery_prohibited|f.reason: Not prohibiting surgery outright (and instead allowing it within education/training and board-authorized regulations) is more permissive than the majority of states (44/50) that explicitly prohibit surgery for optometrists.

profession_specific.systemic_disease_loc.reason: Most states include local manifestations of systemic diseases within podiatric scope. This state explicitly excludes treatment of systemic conditions, narrowing the scope of practice.

profession_specific.systemic_disease_tre.reason: Most states exclude systemic disease treatment from podiatric scope. This state explicitly includes treatment of local manifestations of systemic diseases, expanding the scope of practice.

professional_liability_insurance_require.reason: Most states don't require professional liability insurance for podiatrists. Mandating that all licensed podiatrists providing direct patient care maintain malpractice insurance adds a burden not present in most states.

protected_titles|None.reason: Protecting multiple titles including generic terms like 'Nutritionist' and 'Dietitian' restricts who can use those titles, placing higher barriers on practitioners compared to states that don't address this.

provisional_license_available|None.reason: Offering a provisional license allows practitioners who have completed education but not yet passed exams to begin practicing, lowering the barrier to entry compared to most states that don't provide this option.

provisional_license_duration_months|None.reason: An 18-month provisional license duration is relatively generous, allowing practitioners more time to complete remaining requirements before full licensure, compared to most states that don't address this.

provisional_license_requires_supervision.reason: Requiring provisional license holders to practice only under supervision of a licensed dietitian adds a burden/restriction on provisional practitioners that most states don't impose.

public_health_nurse_certification_availa.reason: Requires a specific state-issued certificate to use the title 'public health nurse' — a credential requirement almost no other state imposes, adding a barrier.

public_liability_insurance_required|None.reason: Explicitly requiring proof of public liability insurance (with a narrow exception for instructors) is an additional burden not addressed by most states, making this more restrictive for practitioners.

public_school_accountant_designation|Non.reason: Requiring a separate public school accountant (PSA) designation to audit school district financials imposes an additional credentialing burden that virtually no other state requires.

qualifier_cessation_notification_days|No.reason: Requiring written notification within 10 days of a qualifier's disassociation is an additional obligation not found in most states, imposing a tight compliance burden on contractors.

qualifier_license_requirement_by_contrac.reason: Requiring a qualifier to hold a specific master electrician license adds a barrier not addressed by most states, making entry more restrictive.

qualifier_license_type_required|None.reason: Specifying that the qualifier must have passed an examination and have HVAC-specific experience is an additional requirement not found in most states, raising the barrier to licensure.

qualifier_replacement_grace_period_days|.reason: A 60-day grace period to replace a qualifier is shorter than the majority value of 90 days, but since most states don't address this at all, the existence of any grace period is permissive relative to no stated allowance. However, compared to the majority (unstated), providing a defined grace period is a neutral-to-permissive structural choice. Given the statute explicitly allows the license to remain in force for 60 days, this is more permissive than having no grace period provision.

qualifier_replacement_notice_days|None.reason: Requiring written notice within 10 days of qualifier cessation imposes a short, strict deadline not found in most states, adding a burden on practitioners.

qualifier_required|None.reason: Mandating a qualifier who must be licensed and hold material authority in the business adds requirements not present in most states, increasing barriers.

rd_credential_accepted_in_lieu_of_state_.reason: Accepting the RD credential in lieu of state requirements provides an alternative pathway to licensure, lowering barriers for already-credentialed practitioners.

referral_to_physician_required|None.reason: Explicitly requiring referral to a physician for certain conditions imposes a duty on optometrists that most states don't codify, adding a compliance obligation.

registered_municipal_accountant_designat.reason: Requiring a separate registered municipal accountant (RMA) designation and examination to audit municipal or county financials imposes an additional credentialing burden that virtually no other state requires.

registration_number_required_in_ads|None.reason: Requiring registration numbers in all advertisements is an additional compliance obligation not addressed by most states, placing a greater burden on contractors.

registration_renewal_interval_years|None.reason: Requiring biennial renewal and mandatory reporting of out-of-state licenses is an additional administrative burden not addressed by most states.

residential_apprentice_supervisor_ratio_.reason: Allowing up to three apprentices per supervisor on residential projects (with potential for more by rule) is a defined allowance that most states don't address; it explicitly permits a relatively generous ratio, reducing restrictions on practitioners.

residential_building_unit_cap|None.reason: This is a definitional/organizational choice setting the scope of residential plumber licenses at up to four units. Most states don't address this cap, and defining the boundary is a structural classification rather than a clear increase or decrease in burden on practitioners.

residential_journeyman_training_program_.reason: Requiring only two years of training for a residential journeyman is less than typical journeyman requirements (often 4 years), making this more permissive for residential-tier licensure.

residential_master_electrician_journeyma.reason: Only two years of experience as a residential journeyman to qualify for residential master electrician is a lower bar than typical master electrician experience requirements, making entry easier.

residential_project_definition|None.reason: This is a definitional/organizational provision clarifying what counts as a residential project; it does not by itself raise or lower barriers to practice.

residential_scope_limited|None.reason: This is a definitional clause establishing a separate residential journeyman plumber classification with limited scope. Most states don't have this distinction; it is an organizational/definitional choice rather than a clear increase or decrease in burden.

residential_wiring_method_restriction|No.reason: This is a definitional provision describing the scope of a residential journeyman license (nonmetallic sheath cable); it is organizational rather than imposing additional burdens.

restorative_function_endorsement_availab.reason: Most states don't offer a restorative function endorsement for dental hygienists. This state creates an additional credential that expands the scope of services hygienists may perform, broadening practice options.

retired_license_status_available|None.reason: Offering a retired license status provides practitioners an additional pathway to maintain a license in a reduced-burden status, which is a benefit/option most states don't provide.

right_of_rescission_days|None.reason: Mandating a 3-business-day right of rescission is an additional consumer-protection requirement not addressed by most states, placing a greater obligation on contractors.

rn_death_pronouncement_authorized|None.reason: Authorizes RNs to pronounce death under specified circumstances, expanding their scope of practice beyond what most states allow.

scope_exclusions|None.reason: Explicitly excluding certain work (unskilled labor, low-hazard cable, class 2/3 circuits, etc.) from the definition of 'electrical trade' reduces the scope of who must be licensed, making the regime more permissive.

scope_expansion_by_rule_authorized|None.reason: Authorizing the division to expand the HVAC contractor's scope of work by rule provides flexibility to broaden what licensees may do, which is more permissive than a fixed, narrower scope.

sedation_adverse_event_reporting_require.reason: Requires mandatory reporting of adverse events (mortality or permanent injury) related to anesthesia/sedation within 30 days, an obligation most states do not explicitly impose.

sedation_anesthesia_permit_types|None.reason: Requires dentists to obtain a specific permit before using general anesthesia on outpatients, an additional authorization requirement most states do not mandate.

sedation_permit_onsite_inspection_requir.reason: Allows the board to require onsite inspection and evaluation before issuing or renewing a sedation/anesthesia permit, adding a potential barrier most states do not have.

self_insurance_permitted|None.reason: Explicitly permitting self-insurance as proof of insurance gives contractors an additional option not available in most states, reducing the barrier to compliance.

sexual_misconduct_training_required|None.reason: Requiring a one-time minimum two-hour training on professional boundaries and sexual misconduct adds a mandatory continuing education burden on all physicians.

small_project_dollar_threshold_exemption.reason: A $7,000 threshold before licensing is required exempts more small projects from regulation compared to states with lower or no thresholds, reducing the number of people who must be licensed.

small_project_dollar_threshold|None.reason: A $7,000 threshold before licensing requirements apply means more small-project workers are exempt from licensing. Most states don't address this threshold at all, and having one (especially for non-electrical/plumbing work) reduces the number of people subject to regulation.

small_project_exemption_threshold_dollar.reason: A $7,000 small-project exemption threshold is not found in most states; it exempts a broad range of projects from licensing requirements, reducing the regulatory burden.

solar_panel_electrical_work_exemption|No.reason: Exempting solar panel workers doing incidental electrical work from licensure requirements reduces barriers for that category of worker.

specialist_license_available|None.reason: Prohibits dentists from advertising as specialists without a state-issued specialist license, adding a licensing requirement for specialty representation that most states do not impose.

specialty_advertising_disclaimer_require.reason: Most states don't require a disclaimer in specialty advertising. This state mandates a clearly distinguishable disclaimer for dentists advertising a practice emphasis without recognized credentials, adding a compliance burden.

specialty_certification_types|None.reason: Requiring optometrists to obtain specialty certification to use therapeutic pharmaceutical agents adds an extra credentialing barrier that most states don't impose.

specialty_practice_scope_restriction|Non.reason: Most states don't restrict a specialist licensee's practice to their specialty. This state limits a specialist's practice to the branch of dentistry in which they hold a specialist license, narrowing their permitted scope.

spectacle_prescription_release_required|.reason: Mandating that optometrists provide written prescriptions to patients upon request imposes an obligation on practitioners that most states don't explicitly require.

state_preempts_local_registration_fees|N.reason: State preemption of local registration fees removes an additional layer of potential fees for contractors, reducing their overall burden compared to states that do not address this.

statute_of_limitations_for_accountant_ne.reason: Establishing a statute of limitations (2 years from discovery or 6 years from service) caps the period during which accountants can be sued for negligence, reducing their legal exposure compared to states that do not address this.

supervised_clinical_internship_required|.reason: Requiring a supervised clinical internship of at least 100 hours certified by a board-certified ophthalmologist adds a significant entry barrier that most states do not impose.

supervision_ratio_limit|None.reason: Capping the number of dietetic technicians a registered dietitian may supervise at two imposes a staffing restriction most states do not have, limiting practice scale.

surgery_definition|None.reason: Defining ophthalmic surgery broadly (including laser ablation and other means) sets a clear boundary that restricts optometrists from performing such procedures, which most states don't explicitly codify.

surgery_prohibited|None.reason: Explicitly prohibiting a broad list of surgical procedures (injections, cataract surgery, laser surgery, etc.) restricts optometrists' scope of practice, which most states don't codify explicitly.

system_components_included|None.reason: Explicitly including the gas line as a component of the HVAC system expands the scope of what requires an HVAC license, potentially restricting who can perform that work without additional credentials.

systemic_disease_local_manifestations_in.reason: Explicitly including treatment of local manifestations of systemic diseases on the foot and ankle expands the permissible scope of podiatric practice beyond what most states define, giving practitioners more latitude.

systemic_disease_treatment_excluded|None.reason: Explicitly excluding treatment of systemic diseases narrows the permissible scope of podiatric practice, restricting what practitioners may do compared to states that do not impose this limitation.

teledentistry_authorized|None.reason: Most states don't explicitly authorize teledentistry. Formally authorizing it expands the modes through which dentists and dental providers may practice, reducing barriers.

telehealth_authorized|None.reason: Most states don't address telehealth. Explicitly authorizing telehealth services expands the options available to practitioners, making it more permissive.

telehealth_practice_authorized|None.reason: Explicitly authorizing telehealth practice expands the modes through which dietitians may practice, reducing barriers compared to states that do not address telehealth.

telehealth_prescribing_rules|None.reason: Requires synchronous audio/audio-visual communication AND a prior in-person encounter within 12 months before a controlled substance can be prescribed via telehealth — stricter than most states which don't address this at all.

telemedicine_authorized|None.reason: Explicitly authorizing telemedicine for optometrists expands the modes of practice available, providing more flexibility than most states which do not address this.

telemedicine_license_available|None.reason: Offering a telemedicine license to out-of-state physicians creates an additional pathway to practice, lowering barriers for those physicians to serve patients in this state.

tibial_pilon_fracture_excluded|None.reason: Most states don't address tibial pilon fractures. Explicitly prohibiting treatment of tibial pilon fractures restricts the scope of practice compared to states that are silent on the matter.

tiered_license_types|None.reason: Creating a tiered 'optometric physician' license with expanded scope provides practitioners a pathway to broader authority, which is more permissive than the single-tier systems most states use.

total_ankle_replacement_authorized|None.reason: Most states don't address total ankle replacement. Explicitly authorizing it (with documentation requirements) expands the scope of practice for qualifying podiatrists.

utility_worker_exemption|None.reason: Exempting utility workers, railroad, telephone, elevator, and municipal utility employees from electrician licensure reduces the population subject to licensing requirements.

vaccination_authority|None.reason: Explicitly granting podiatrists vaccination authority expands their scope of practice beyond what most states address, reducing barriers and increasing what they are permitted to do.

vision_therapy_authorized|None.reason: Explicitly authorizing vision therapy expands the scope of practice for optometrists, granting additional authority that most states don't address.

voidable_contract_clauses|None.reason: Specifying that certain contract clauses make the contract voidable by the owner imposes additional restrictions on contractors' contract terms not addressed by most states.

voltage_limit_residential|None.reason: This is a definitional boundary for the residential project category; it clarifies scope but does not by itself impose additional burdens on practitioners.

weight_control_program_exemption|None.reason: Providing an exemption for weight control programs supervised by or approved by a registered dietitian reduces the scope of who must be licensed, making the regulatory environment more permissive for those offering such programs.

whistleblower_protection_for_delegation_.reason: Protects nurses from retaliation for refusing improperly delegated tasks — reduces burden/risk on practitioners and most states don't provide this protection.

workers_compensation_insurance_required|.reason: Requiring proof of workers' compensation insurance as a condition of licensure adds a financial/administrative burden not universally required by most states.

wound_debridement_authorized|None.reason: Authorizing wound debridement on limbs and torso expands the scope of podiatric practice beyond the foot and ankle, which is more permissive than most states that don't address this.

xray_technician_certification_required|N.reason: The statute requires X-ray technicians in podiatrist offices to obtain a certificate of proficiency from the board, an additional credentialing burden that most states do not impose.
